title: Georgia: Five minutes from dictatorship? – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: An ECFR podcast on Georgia two years after a disputed election: Ketevan Bolkvadze argues the country is consolidating into an electoral authoritarian state, while Sergi Kapanadze warns it is 'five minutes away' from dictatorship as Georgian Dream moves to ban major opposition groups. Civic mobilisation persists but is not translating into institutional change, and ties with Brussels are deteriorating.

insights.claim: Two years after a disputed parliamentary election, Georgia is moving further from Europe as Georgian Dream seeks to ban major opposition groups and tighten its grip on political life.
insights.speaker: Ketevan Bolkvadze, Jessica Hendrick, Sergi Kapanadze
insights.so_what: Georgia's EU path is effectively stalled, raising political risk for investors in the Caucasus corridor.

insights.claim: Ketevan Bolkvadze argues Georgia is no longer simply experiencing 'authoritarian drift' but is increasingly consolidating into an electoral authoritarian state.
insights.speaker: Ketevan Bolkvadze
insights.so_what: Treat Georgia's governance trajectory as entrenched rather than cyclical.
insights.locator: In this episode, Jessica Hendrick welcomes

insights.claim: Sergi Kapanadze warns Georgia remains 'five minutes away' from dictatorship because Georgian Dream is moving to eliminate not only parties but the wider network of politicians, civil society groups and media able to challenge it.
insights.speaker: Sergi Kapanadze
insights.so_what: Elimination of independent media and civil society reduces transparency and rule-of-law protections.
insights.locator: In this episode, Jessica Hendrick welcomes

insights.claim: Trust in Georgia's government and political parties is collapsing even as civic mobilisation endures, yet that mobilisation is not translating into institutional change.
insights.speaker: Ketevan Bolkvadze, Jessica Hendrick, Sergi Kapanadze
insights.so_what: Sustained protest without a political outlet implies prolonged instability rather than a reset.

themes.theme: EU leverage over a reluctant candidate

insights.claim: The discussion raises whether Georgia built state capacity faster than democratic safeguards, and what the EU can do when a candidate country's government no longer appears to want membership.
insights.speaker: Ketevan Bolkvadze, Jessica Hendrick, Sergi Kapanadze
insights.so_what: EU enlargement leverage is weak where governments no longer seek accession.
